title: Square-root growth of operator entanglement in an integrable brickwork circuit
abstract: It is widely expected that the von Neumann entanglement of a local operator grows at most logarithmically in integrable many-body systems in infinite volume. We give a counterexample in a four-state brickwork circuit whose gate is a permutation matrix solving the constant Yang--Baxter equation. The von Neumann operator entropy grows as $(\log2)\sqrt{t/π}+O(\log t)$, whereas fixed-index Rényi entropies grow linearly below index one and logarithmically above it. At fixed relative Hilbert--Schmidt error below one, matrix product operator simulations require a bond dimension growing at least as $\exp(c\sqrt t)$ for some $c>0$.
summary: This work investigates the entanglement growth of local operators in an integrable quantum circuit, demonstrating that the entanglement scales superlogarithmically ($\propto \sqrt{t}$) rather than the expected logarithmic rate. By constructing a specific integrable model, the authors show that simulating the time evolution requires an exponentially growing bond dimension, challenging current theoretical bounds on entanglement in such systems.
main_problem: The paper challenges the long-standing expectation that operator entanglement in integrable many-body systems grows at most logarithmically with time.
main_result: The von Neumann operator entropy grows superlogarithmically, specifically as $\sqrt{t}$, and the required bond dimension for MPO simulation grows exponentially as $\exp(c\sqrt{t})$.
method: The analysis uses the 'folding trick' to map Heisenberg evolution to Schrödinger evolution, employing techniques from tensor networks and asymptotic analysis (Central Limit Theorem) to bound entanglement measures.
model_or_system: The model is a four-state brickwork circuit on an infinite chain, governed by a specific permutation matrix gate that ensures Yang-Baxter integrability.
key_observables: Von Neumann operator entropy ($S_{	ext{op}, 1}$), Rényi entropies ($S_{	ext{op}, \alpha}$), and the required bond dimension ($\chi(t)$) for MPO simulation.
important_parameters: Time ($t$), Rényi index ($\alpha$), and the bond dimension $\chi$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system size $L 	o \infty$ at fixed time $t$, and the MPO bound relies on the Central Limit Theorem for the count imbalance.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the braid representation of the circuit, the setup for state/operator entanglement across a cut, and the entanglement structure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first analyzing state entanglement, then developing the 'folding trick' to tackle operator entanglement, deriving the $\sqrt{t}$ scaling for entropy, and finally establishing the exponential lower bound on the MPO bond dimension.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete counterexample to a major conjecture in the field of integrable quantum systems, showing that entanglement scaling can be much faster than previously thought, which has implications for understanding quantum thermalization and complexity.
